Coastal property values could erode if nourishment subsidies end

At first glance, one might think this is about the US Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP), also known by the old term "food stamps." But the "nourishment" referred to in the article is actually new sand transported to beaches from elsewhere to replace sand that has been removed by natural erosion.

from the article:
In beach nourishment, new sand, often dredged from nearby inlets or the offshore sea floor, is added to an eroding beach to widen it and help prevent future erosion. "The expectation that the federal government will continue to provide subsidies for erosion-control measures has significantly inflated property values in many coastal communities," said Dylan E. McNamara, associate professor of physics and physical oceanography at the University of North Carolina Wilmington. "If these subsidies were suddenly removed, our model suggests values could experience a rapid and dramatic adjustment downward."
